== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== con-leche/ConLeche/Verify/Cached/MainC.lean#L36-L42
    36  /-- **Acceptance**: what the fold accepts carries the model. -/
    37  theorem checkDecls_sound (hμ : μ.verifiedChecks = true)
    38      {ds : Array Declaration} {env' : Env}
    39      (h : checkDecls μ pins ds = .ok env') :
    40      Nonempty (EnvModelM V μ env') := by
    41    obtain ⟨fc, rfl⟩ := checkDecls_fullyChecked μ h
    42    exact fullyChecked_sound V hμ fc

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L87-L209
    87  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
    88                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    89                 FILE.ndjson
    90         con-ron --help
    91  
    92    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    93    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    94    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    95    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    96    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    97    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    98    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
    99    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   100    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   101  
   102    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   103                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   104                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   105                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  The
   106                      same two statements are PROVED about this program's
   107                      pipeline (ConRon.Capstone.model_exists and
   108                      no_False_declaration, on the Aeneas model of the Rust),
   109                      using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and
   110                      Quot.sound.  What they still assume are hypotheses, not
   111                      axioms: that the driver runs the extracted stages in the
   112                      order it does on the file's bytes.  They hold at every pin
   113                      text and every prelude.  OVERVIEW.md section 3.1 lists
   114                      them.
   115    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   116                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   117                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   118    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   119                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   120                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   121                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   122                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   123                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   124                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   125                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   126                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   127                      error, as in con-leche.
   128    --no-mark-persistent
   129                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP, for a stronger reason than the
   130                      `con-ron` binary's: the mark it turns off is a
   131                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   132                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this checker has no
   133                      reference counts at all -- a term is a u32 handle into a
   134                      Vec and the persistent tier is immutable in phase B.  A
   135                      run that passes it says so on stderr.
   136    --progress[=<stride>]
   137                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   138                      phase:
   139                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   140                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   141                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> pending
   142                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   143                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   144                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s
   145                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   146                      declaration is installed, so a run that dies in the
   147                      install phase names the declaration it died in on its last
   148                      line; a check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th
   149                      COMPLETED check.  On a failure the phase's closing line
   150                      says so and the summary still prints.  Bare --progress is
   151                      stride 1; a stride that is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is
   152                      a usage error.
   153    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   154                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   155                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.  The pins
   156                      are interned into the persistent tier at startup, before
   157                      the fold (DESIGN.md section 8.6 P2d).
   158    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   159                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   160                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   161                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   162                      verified core and decoded by it.  A run with either
   163                      flag is outside the proved theorems.
   164    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   165                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   166                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   167                      measurement can be reproduced.
   168  
   169  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   170  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   171  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   172  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   173  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   174  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   175  
   176  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   177  exits 3 without reading its input.
   178  
   179  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   180  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   181  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   182  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   183  
   184  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   185  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   186  built-in prelude's own records are not counted; a stream record that declares
   187  a prelude declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the
   188  number of environment CONSTANTS is not.
   189  
   190  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   191  checker's own little prelude -- the five pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, Empty,
   192  False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   193  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   194  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   195  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   196  hash-consed together.
   197  
   198  NO PREPROCESSOR, NO MODELS.  The input is a RAW lean4export stream: there is no
   199  external tool, no dependency and no spawn.  Every inductive block --
   200  structures, sums, indexed families, recursive, reflexive, mutual and nested
   201  blocks -- is installed by the ONE uniform installer: it checks the type formers
   202  and constructors, runs the positivity check, and GENERATES the block's
   203  recursors; the stream's recursor records supply only their types, compared with
   204  the generated ones up to definitional equality, and their classes -- the rule
   205  bodies the stream carries are ignored.  No model is ever read from the input: a
   206  stream record whose name carries a `_model` component is an ordinary
   207  declaration with no effect on any block.  A block whose shape the installer
   208  does not recognise declines (exit 2), naming it.  The binary reads no
   209  environment variable.";

    19  //! |---|---|---|

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L13-L132
    13  /-!
    14  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    15  
    16  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    17  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    18  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    19  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    20  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    21  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    22  
    23  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    24    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    25  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    26    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    30  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    31  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§5's census).  What they
    32  still assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    33  
    34  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    35  
    36  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    37  around six extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    38  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    39  
    40      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    41        → prepare_prelude → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    42  
    43  The headlines (§4) take one premise per call, from the binary's own start
    44  values `startState`/`emptyTier` (§3); §4's table maps each premise to its line
    45  of `check_main`.
    46  
    47  and the twin runs the same six stages (`Arena/Main.lean`'s
    48  `runPipelineHead`/`runPipelineTail` drive them for `con-ron-lean`).  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    49  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    50  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    51  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::parallel_all`, and thaws the tier.
    52  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` phase A, `h7` the freeze, `h8`
    53  phase B), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    54  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  Phase B's premise `h8` is
    55  the contract of the generic combinator `pool::parallel_all` with the driver's
    56  two verified closures, written out (task #98-H8): index lists `ws`, one per
    57  worker, covering every pending record, and for each a `foldlM` of
    58  `check_pending` over its indices from `worker_state`, accepting.  That
    59  contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    60  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.  `parallelAll_of_pool` reads it as
    61  `Phased.lean`'s `ParallelAll`, and `PoolAccepts.toParts` turns that into one
    62  accepting fold per worker over the records it checked.
    63  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    64  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    65  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    66  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    67  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as premises (that the binary's
    68  `check_main` makes exactly these calls, in this order, is the one trusted
    69  line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and the proof is:
    70  
    71  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    72     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    73     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    74     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    75  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    76     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    77     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    78     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    79     (`stages_no_False`, through the pure fold);
    80  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    81     model.
    82  
    83  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    84  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    85  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    86  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    87  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    88  
    89  ## The named hypotheses
    90  
    91  Since task #98-HEADLINE the headlines start from the binary's own start
    92  values (`startState` = `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`)
    93  instead of quantifying over a start state with `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`
    94  equations, name the call the binary makes at each step (`prepare_d`, not
    95  `prepare_prelude`).  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    96  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    97  they assume is exactly:
    98  
    99  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   100    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   101    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   102    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   103    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   104    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam — the one seam left.
   105  
   106  Former hypotheses, now theorems or gone (DESIGN.md's task #97-COMPOSE and
   107  #98-HEADLINE sections tag each with its owning lane):
   108

    34  def ReadsAs {S : Type} (inst : frontend.export_c.ChunkSource S) :
    35      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop
    36    | src, [] => ∃ e src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (e, src') ∧ e.val = []
    37    | src, c :: cs => c.val ≠ [] ∧
    38        ∃ src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (c, src') ∧ ReadsAs inst src' cs

     5  //!
     6  //! ```text
     7  //! bits 31…28   ctor tag   (4 bits, high)

    13  //! the tier *above* the index rather than in the low bit (con-leche's lesson
    14  //! 6) — a persistent handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3737-L3772
  3737  
  3738      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:472-492 EStore.intern
  3739      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3740      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3741      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3742      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3743      ///
  3744      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3745      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3746      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3747      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3748      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3749      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3750      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3751      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3752      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3753      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3754      ///
  3755      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3756      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3757      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3758      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3759          match v {
  3760              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3761              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3762              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3763              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3764              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3765              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3766              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3767              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3768              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3769              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3770          }
  3771      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L4022-L4068
  4022      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4023          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  4024          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  4025              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  4026                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  4027              } else {
  4028                  true
  4029              }
  4030          } else {
  4031              false
  4032          };
  4033          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  4034              None
  4035          } else if pers.frozen {
  4036              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  4037          } else {
  4038              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  4039          };
  4040          match hit {
  4041              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  4042              None => {
  4043                  if self.scratch_on {
  4044                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  4045                      match at.1 {
  4046                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  4047                          None => {
  4048                              if self.scr.apps.full() {
  4049                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4050                              } else {
  4051                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4052                                  let h: EIdx =
  4053                                      EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  4054                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  4055                                  Ok(h)
  4056                              }
  4057                          }
  4058                      }
  4059                  } else if self.pers.apps.full() {
  4060                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4061                  } else {
  4062                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4063                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  4064                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  4065                      Ok(h)
  4066                  }
  4067              }
  4068          }

 10118  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:313-320 CState.flushed
 10119  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3580-3586 flushCaches` — **what
 10120  /// the per-declaration bracket does to the caches**: it drops them whole,
 10121  /// which is con-leche's own `flushC`, the operation its driver runs at exactly
 10122  /// this point.
 10123  ///
 10124  /// Task #97-P4c ported DESIGN.md §8.3's survivor policy instead — keep the
 10125  /// rows whose key AND value are persistent — which is sound and strictly more
 10126  /// caching; task #97f measured what it costs (`filter` is `O(table)` and the
 10127  /// survivors accumulate, so the fold pays `O(declarations × surviving rows)`:
 10128  /// 16 % of `Init`'s first 4 380 declarations' cycles, 213 s → 124 s).  The
 10129  /// twin's `Caches.dropScratchEntries` stays as the SPECIFICATION of a
 10130  /// surviving row, and so does `Caches::drop_scratch_entries` below it with
 10131  /// its eleven journals — P3 needs it to state that flushing is sound.
 10132  pub fn flush_caches(st: &mut AState) {
 10133      st.caches.reset();
 10134  }
 10135  
 10136  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10137  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3588-3596 dropScratch` — drop the
 10138  /// scratch tier of the store and the cache entries that name it, in one
 10139  /// operation, so the two halves cannot drift apart; and **thaw** the store:
 10140  /// the tier `enter_scratch` handed out comes back (task #98-FREEZE), so the
 10141  /// store is owned and scratch-off again.
 10142  pub fn drop_scratch(st: &mut AState, tier: PersTier) {
 10143      flush_caches(st);
 10144      st.store.thaw(tier);
 10145  }
 10146  
 10147  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, opened** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 10148  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3598-3605 enterScratch` — turn the
 10149  /// scratch tier on, and clear the per-call memo tables of `Memos`, which
 10150  /// belong to no tier and whose keys the new tier may reuse.  **Opening a
 10151  /// bracket is freezing the store** (task #98-FREEZE): its persistent tables
 10152  /// are handed back as the `PersTier` every read inside the bracket goes
 10153  /// through and promotion writes, and every append inside it is a scratch
 10154  /// append.
 10155  pub fn enter_scratch(st: &mut AState) -> PersTier {
 10156      st.memos.reset();
 10157      st.store.freeze()
 10158  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/promote.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! `arena::promote` — the scratch → persistent copy (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-2).
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Promote.lean`, declaration for
     4  //! declaration, under DESIGN.md §8.6's lockstep ruling.
     5  //!
     6  //! DESIGN.md §8.3, "**Phase A runs in the scratch tier too, with promotion**":
     7  //!
     8  //! > The install phase (annotate the type and the value, infer, defeq) was
     9  //! > interning every intermediate into the persistent tier — on `Init` 5.06 M
    10  //! > permanent nodes on top of the parse's 6.14 M (+82 %) […].  The arena's
    11  //! > answer is con-leche #64's: phase A opens the scratch tier like phase B,
    12  //! > and the two handles it must keep (the annotated type, the annotated
    13  //! > value) are **promoted** — a memoised structural copy scratch →
    14  //! > persistent […] before the tier is dropped.  Persistent handles are
    15  //! > promoted to themselves.
    16  //!
    17  //! This module is that copy, at all four handle kinds and lifted to
    18  //! `arena::env`'s declaration layer, plus `promote_new` — the entry
    19  //! `arena::checker`'s two fold steps call, which promotes a step's NEWLY
    20  //! INSTALLED constants in place.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## What it is
    23  //!
    24  //! `view` the node, promote its children, `intern` the result into the
    25  //! PERSISTENT tier (`arena::store`'s `intern_persistent` family, whose section
    26  //! note carries the WF obligations).  Three properties make it cheap and make
    27  //! it right:
    28  //!
    29  //! * **a persistent handle promotes to itself**, by one tier-bit test
    30  //!   (`is_persistent`) and no store access at all.  Most of what a step
    31  //!   leaves behind IS the parsed term (since task #119 a value kind's record
    32  //!   is exactly the parsed one), so the walk stops at the first persistent
    33  //!   node on every branch;
    34  //! * **the memo makes it `O(result)`** and not `O(unfolding)`: the subject is
    35  //!   a hash-consed DAG, and an unmemoised structural copy of a DAG is the
    36  //!   mistake task #97g's item 5 found three times over.  The memo is per
    37  //!   DECLARATION — a scratch handle means nothing once the tier is dropped —
    38  //!   and it is threaded as an argument-and-result pair, a moved
    39  //!   `ron::HashMap` returned, which is `frontend::proj_rec`'s spelling for its
    40  //!   `seen` set and `arena::expr_ops`' for the three memoized scope walks;

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L612-L634
   612  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
   613  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its phase-B worker reads the
   614  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Phased.lean`).
   615  /// **The persistent tier out of the store and into a value** (task
   616  /// #97-P6-6b's driver function, moved here by task #97-P5-Driver): the four
   617  /// persistent tables move into one `PersTier` handed back `frozen`, for the
   618  /// phase-B workers to read.  Task #98-FREEZE: this is a pure MOVE — the
   619  /// store's scratch tiers and flags are untouched (a worker's store is its own,
   620  /// `worker_state`), there is no flag to test and so no decline (`M_REFREEZE`
   621  /// is gone), and `thaw_tier` puts the tables back where they were.  The
   622  /// driver's store is not read between the two.
   623  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore) -> PersTier {
   624      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
   625      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
   626      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
   627      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
   628      PersTier {
   629          frozen: true,
   630          n,
   631          l,
   632          ls,
   633          e,
   634      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L444-L491
   444  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   445  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   446  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   447  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   448  
   449  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:395-397 Expr.allLevelParamsDefinedFast
   450  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/DeclCheck.lean:190-192 Expr.constsResolveFFast
   451  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   452  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   453  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   454  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   455  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   456  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   457  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   458  ///
   459  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   460  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   461  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   462  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   463  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   464  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   465  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   466  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   467  ///
   468  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   469  /// |---|---:|
   470  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   471  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   472  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   473  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   474  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   475  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   476  ///
   477  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   478  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   479  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   480  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   481  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   482  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   483      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   484      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   485          HashMap::new()
   486      } else {
   487          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   488          reset_map(&mut m2);
   489          m2
   490      }
   491  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L351-L538

   394      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   395      // ConRon.Capstone: h2
   396      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &mut st) {
   397          Ok(p) => p,
   398          Err((e, line)) => {
   399              let what = match classify(&e) {
   400                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   401                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   402                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   403              };
   404              eprintln!(
   405                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   406                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   407                  what, mode_tag
   408              );
   409              return 3;
   410          }
   411      };
   412      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   413      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   414      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   415      // store above.  No model is ever read from the input: every inductive
   416      // block — mutual and nested included — installs through the kernel's
   417      // uniform installer, unconditionally (task #105).
   418      // ConRon.Capstone: hreads, h3 (`parse_source` over the file's handle)
   419      let parsed: ParseResultD = match driver::parse_export_stream_d(
   420          pers,
   421          &mut st,
   422          file,
   423          export_c::CHUNK_SIZE,
   424      ) {
   425          Err(e) => {
   426              eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", file, e);
   427              return 3;
   428          }
   429          Ok((Err((e, line)), _)) => match classify(&e) {
   430              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   431                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   432                  return 2;
   433              }
   434              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   435              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   436              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   437                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   438                  return 1;
   439              }
   440              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   441                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", file, line, msg);
   442                  return 3;
   443              }
   444          },
   445          Ok((Ok(r), _)) => r,
   446      };
   447      let file_records = parsed.decls.len();
   448      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   449      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   450      // produced indexes into it.
   451      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   452      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   453      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   454      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   455      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   456      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   457      // ConRon.Capstone: h4
   458      let prepared = match prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed.decls) {
   459          Ok(p) => p,
   460          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   461      };
   462      // the ground hoist's receipt
   463      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   464          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   465              .hoisted
   466              .iter()
   467              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   468              .collect();
   469          eprintln!(
   470              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   471               they ground: {}",
   472              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   473              names.join(", ")
   474          );
   475      }
   476      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   477      // outside the theorems)
   478      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {
   479          Ok(p) => p,
   480          Err(e) => {
   481              eprintln!("con-ron: {}", e);
   482              return 3;
   483          }
   484      };
   485      // The heartbeat's first line: the parse and the preparation are done.
   486      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(a.progress, t0);
   487      hb.parse_done(
   488          prepared.decls.len(),
   489          file_records,
   490          prepared.synthesised,
   491          (
   492              st.store.node_count(pers),
   493              st.store.ls().node_count(pers),
   494              st.store.ns().node_count(pers),
   495          ),
   496      );
   497      // **THE STARTUP PIN WALK** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d): every
   498      // pinned datum the checker compares a stream record against — the six
   499      // basis blocks in both forms, the axiom pins, the reserved names and the
   500      // `Nat`-operation variants — interned ONCE, here, while the scratch tier
   501      // is still off, so that nothing the fold compares against lives in a tier
   502      // that is about to vanish.  Its result is the fold's pin parameter.
   503      // ConRon.Capstone: h5
   504      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(pers, &mut st, &pins) {
   505          Ok(p) => p,
   506          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   507      };
   508      // ONE driver, and the heartbeat is printed between its steps
   509      // (`driver::check_decls_driver`: phase A, the frozen tier, and the pool
   510      // for its phase B).
   511      let jobs: u64 = match a.jobs {
   512          Some(n) => n,
   513          None => con_ron::driver::default_jobs(),
   514      };
   515      // ONE lane, whatever the flags: the driver is what freezes the persistent
   516      // tier at the phase boundary and phase B is the pool at every worker count
   517      // (task #97-P6-6b), so a run with no heartbeat is the same computation as
   518      // a run with one and `install_then_check` is no longer a second path.
   519      // ConRon.Capstone: h6, h7, h8 (the driver's three steps, either observer)
   520      let verdict = if a.progress > 0 {
   521          driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, &prepared.decls, jobs, &mut hb)
   522      } else {
   523          let mut silent = driver::Silent;
   524          driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, &prepared.decls, jobs, &mut silent)
   525      };
   526      // **The headline number is the FILE's declaration-record count**: the
   527      // records the PARSE produced, which are the file's own.  Nothing the
   528      // preparation does moves it.
   529      let stream_records = file_records as u64;
   530      let code = match &verdict {
   531          Ok(_) => driver::verdict_accept(stream_records, mode_tag),
   532          Err((e, i)) => {
   533              driver::verdict_failure(pers, &st.store, &prepared.decls, e, *i, mode_tag, t0)
   534          }
   535      };
   536      exit_after_verdict(code)
   537  }
   538  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:115-132 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is (`arena/env.rs`'s `table_name` note).
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

   689  /// a stream record against, interned into the tier that is live at the call —

   693  /// `quot_pin_hit` compare against, the STORED ones `check_basis_decl`
   694  /// installs), the standard and compiler-trust axiom pins, the reserved names
   695  /// the guards compare by handle, and the `Nat`-operation pin variants, whose

   697  pub fn intern_all_pins(
   698      pers: &PersTier,
   699      st: &mut AState,
   700      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,
   701  ) -> Result<Vec<INatOpPinSet>, CheckError> {

   708                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
   709              },
   710          },
   711      }
   712  }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L931-L976
   931  // handle.  Only the READS are here, for `crate::driver`'s reason:
   932  // `IO.FS.Handle.read` has no model, and a theorem about the file is a
   933  // theorem about its bytes.
   934  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   935  
   936  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/Stream.lean:297-311 serialLoop
   937  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   938  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   939  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   940  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   941  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   942  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   943  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   944      /// The open reader.
   945      pub h: &'a mut R,
   946      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   947      pub chunk: usize,
   948      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   949      pub chunks: u64,
   950      /// The first read failure, if any.
   951      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   952  }
   953  
   954  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/Stream.lean:297-311 serialLoop
   955  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   956      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/Stream.lean:297-311 serialLoop
   957      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   958      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   959          if self.err.is_some() {
   960              return Vec::new();
   961          }
   962          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   963          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   964              Ok(n) => {
   965                  buf.truncate(n);
   966                  if n > 0 {
   967                      self.chunks += 1;
   968                  }
   969                  buf
   970              }
   971              Err(e) => {
   972                  self.err = Some(e);
   973                  Vec::new()
   974              }
   975          }
   976      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1-L41
     1  //! `arena::checker` — the declaration fold, over handles.
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean`, which is con-leche's
     4  //! `Kernel/Checker.lean`'s `checkDecl`/`checkDeclsPure` and
     5  //! `Cached/Installed.lean`'s two-phase `checkDecls`.
     6  //!
     7  //! ## Two folds, and which is which
     8  //!
     9  //! * **`check_decls_pure`** is the THEOREM's shape —
    10  //!   `ConLeche/Model/Fold.lean`'s `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` consumes it, and
    11  //!   DESIGN.md §8.2's Theorem 1 folds `checkDecl` over the stream.  One step
    12  //!   per record, install and check together.
    13  //! * **`install_then_check`** is what the BINARY runs: phase A installs every
    14  //!   record, guarding its header and its value but not inferring; phase B
    15  //!   checks each recorded declaration against the PREFIX VIEW it was installed
    16  //!   at.  con-leche proves the two are the same accept
    17  //!   (`fullyChecked_checkDecls`); the arena's two call the same `checkDecl`
    18  //!   pieces, which is what keeps them the same computation.
    19  //!
    20  //! ## Every step is bracketed
    21  //!
    22  //! DESIGN.md §8.3: "Persistent = parse + installed environment; scratch = one
    23  //! declaration's check."  Both phases and both folds run each record inside
    24  //! `enter_scratch` … `drop_scratch`.  Phase B's `check_pending` brackets
    25  //! `check_value_group`, and every node it appends goes with the tier.  Phase
    26  //! A's `install_step` brackets the install too (the fallback
    27  //! `install_step_other` included), because the ordinary step's installers
    28  //! infer and inference interns: `promote` copies exactly what leaves the step
    29  //! — the installed constants and the pending record — to the persistent tier
    30  //! before the drop (see `install_step`).
    31  //! `check_decls_pure`'s step, `check_decl_step`, is bracketed the same way.
    32  //!
    33  //! ## The pins are interned at startup
    34  //!
    35  //! `intern_all_pins` is DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d's one-time tree walk, and it is what
    36  //! makes every later `pin`/`intern_ci` of the same datum return the PERSISTENT
    37  //! handle whatever tier is live (§8.3: `intern` probes the persistent table
    38  //! first).  Without it a reserved name first interned inside a scratch tier
    39  //! would compare unequal to the stream's own persistent copy of it, which is
    40  //! the one way hash-consing can go wrong across the tier boundary.
    41  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L184-L240
   184  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:135-173 installStepC
   185  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:153-207 installStep` — **phase
   186  /// A's step, bracketed**; `i` is the fold position the record is tagged with.
   187  ///
   188  /// **The bracket** (DESIGN.md §8.3, "Phase A runs in the scratch tier too,
   189  /// with promotion", task #97-P6-2):
   190  ///
   191  /// ```text
   192  /// flush_caches; enter_scratch; <the step>; promote; drop_scratch
   193  /// ```
   194  ///
   195  /// `promote` (`arena::promote`) is the memoised structural copy scratch →
   196  /// persistent, run on **exactly what leaves the step**: the `k` constants the
   197  /// step installed (`promote_new`) and the pending record (`promote_vg`, at the
   198  /// SAME memo).  A persistent handle promotes to itself, so a record that
   199  /// installs what the parse already built — every value kind since task #119,
   200  /// whose install half interns nothing — pays one tier-bit test per handle;
   201  /// the blocks the ordinary step installs (inductives, the basis) still build
   202  /// terms.  The flush stays where con-leche puts it, at the head
   203  /// (`installGuardsC` and the `.thmDecl` arm's own `flushC`, and
   204  /// `checkDeclStepC`'s), so every phase-A record starts with EMPTY caches.
   205  pub fn install_step(
   206      _pers: &PersTier,
   207      st: &mut AState,
   208      mode: &CheckMode,
   209      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   210      i: u64,
   211      fe: IFEnv,
   212      pend: Vec<PendingCheck>,
   213      pd: &IDeclaration,
   214  ) -> Result<(IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>), CheckError> {
   215      let vis: u64 = fe.visible_below;
   216      flush_caches(st);
   217      let mut tier: PersTier = enter_scratch(st);
   218      match install_step_go(&tier, st, mode, pins, fe, pd) {
   219          Err(e) => {
   220              drop_scratch(st, tier);
   221              Err(e)
   222          }
   223          Ok((fe2, vg_opt)) => {
   224              let k: u64 = fe2.visible_below - vis;
   225              match vg_opt {
   226                  None => match promote_new(&mut tier, st, PMemo::empty(), CORE_WALK_FUEL, k, fe2) {
   227                      Err(e) => {
   228                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   229                          Err(e)
   230                      }
   231                      Ok((_, fe3)) => {
   232                          drop_scratch(st, tier);
   233                          Ok((fe3, pend))
   234                      }
   235                  },
   236                  Some(vg) => install_step_promote(tier, st, i, vis, k, fe2, pend, vg),
   237              }
   238          }
   239      }
   240  }

   533      pers: &PersTier,

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L529-L622
   529  
   530  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:431-448 checkDecls
   531  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Run.lean:85-234 checkDeclsIO
   532  /// **The driver**: the two-phase fold with the boundary visible — a straight
   533  /// line of calls, with the observer's lines between them and the pool for
   534  /// phase B (tasks #97-P5-Driver, #98-POOL).  Each step is one premise of the capstone:
   535  ///
   536  /// | step | here | the capstone's premise |
   537  /// |---|---|---|
   538  /// | phase A | `checker::install_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call accepts |
   539  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call's value |
   540  /// | phase B | `pool::parallel_all(m, workers, ‖ worker_state(pins), ‖w, k‖ check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]), …)` | `h8`: index lists `ws` covering `0..pend.len`, each `w` a `foldlM` of `check_pending tier st mode fe pend[k]` over `k ∈ w` from `worker_state pins`, accepting (internally `ParallelAll`) |
   541  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | restores the store (`freeze_tier_ok`) |
   542  ///
   543  /// `init` and `step` are calls into the verified crate; `parallel_all` is the
   544  /// one trusted piece, and its contract (`pool.rs`'s note) is exactly
   545  /// `ParallelAll`: on `Ok`, every record was checked by some worker,
   546  /// each worker folding `check_pending` over the records it claimed on ONE
   547  /// `worker_state`.  Everything else here is the observer, which only ever
   548  /// holds `&` the state (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the
   549  /// other lines through `&st.store` and the worker's `&AState`), so it cannot
   550  /// change an outcome.
   551  ///
   552  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN** (task #97-P6-6b).  Phase A
   553  /// owns its persistent tier and appends to it; at the boundary
   554  /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves the four stores' persistent tables out into
   555  /// one `PersTier`, handed back `frozen`: every read through it goes to those
   556  /// tables, and a worker's own store is frozen (`checker::worker_state`), so
   557  /// every append there is a scratch append (task #98-FREEZE).  The
   558  /// installed index goes to the workers by reference, since `check_pending`
   559  /// takes the visibility bound as a scalar — so `n` workers share one
   560  /// environment and one term DAG and own nothing but a scratch tier, their
   561  /// caches and a copy of the pin handles (`checker::worker_state`).
   562  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   563      pers: &PersTier,
   564      st: &mut AState,
   565      mode: &CheckMode,
   566      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   567      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   568      jobs: u64,
   569      obs: &mut O,
   570  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   571      let total = ds.len();
   572      // PHASE A (ConRon.Capstone: h6): the verified fold, the heartbeat as hook.
   573      let p = match checker::install_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   574          Err(e) => {
   575              obs.install_failed(e.1, total);
   576              return Err(e);
   577          }
   578          Ok(p) => p,
   579      };
   580      let (_n_installed, fe, pend): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>) = p;
   581      let m = pend.len();
   582      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m);
   583      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   584      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   585      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier leaves the state and becomes a
   586      // value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   587      // (empty) store, its tables moved out, so the observer can still read a
   588      // label back through the tier.  (ConRon.Capstone: h7)
   589      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store);
   590      // PHASE B: `check_pending` at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   591      // folding it over the records it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the
   592      // verdict and the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at
   593      // every `--jobs` (the least failing index).  (ConRon.Capstone: h8)
   594      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   595      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   596      let r = parallel_all(
   597          m,
   598          workers,
   599          || checker::worker_state(&st.pins),
   600          |w: &mut AState, k| checker::check_pending(&tier, w, mode, &fe, &pend[k]),
   601          |w: &AState, k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, w, m, &pend[k]),
   602      );
   603      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   604          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   605          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   606      };
   607      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   608      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   609      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   610      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   611      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   612      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   613      checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   614      match phase_b_verdict(&pend, r) {
   615          Err((e, pos)) => {
   616              obs.check_failed(pos);
   617              Err((e, pos))
   618          }
   619          Ok(()) => {
   620              obs.check_done(m);
   621              Ok(fe)
   622          }

    30  //! ## What a worker is, in phase B
    31  //!
    32  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what phase B is: "the persistent tier is immutable
    33  //! in phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**",
    34  //! and task #97-P6-6 verified it in the code (`check_pending` is the bracket;
    35  //! the persistent interns' only caller is phase A's `arena::promote`, which
    36  //! writes a `&mut PersTier` a worker never holds).  So the driver's `init`
    37  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN
    38  //! (`EStore::empty_frozen`: every append a scratch append), its own `Memos`
    39  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    40  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier` and
    41  //! the installed `&IFEnv` (by reference: `check_pending` takes the record's
    42  //! prefix bound as a scalar, `pc.vis`, so a worker costs no environment copy
    43  //! at all — task #97-P6-6b).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L666-L679
   666  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:180-196 checkWorker
   667  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:29-36 AState.worker` — the twin's
   668  /// phase-B worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
   669  /// **A phase-B worker's start state** (task #97-P6-6b's `pool::worker_state`,

   671  /// (`EStore::empty_frozen`, task #98-FREEZE), so that every persistent read

   674  /// frozen for the worker's life: `check_pending` only empties its scratch tier.
   675  pub fn worker_state(pins: &Pins) -> AState {
   676      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty_frozen());
   677      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);
   678      st
   679  }

   227  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:207-245 checkPool
   228  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   229  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   230  ///
   231  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by exactly one
   232  /// > worker, each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step`
   233  /// > over its claimed indices in claim order (increasing), and every step
   234  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   235  ///
   236  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   237  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   238  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   239  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   240  ///
   241  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   242  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   243  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   244  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   245  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   246  /// not depend on it.
   247  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   248      n: usize,
   249      workers: usize,
   250      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   251      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   252      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   253  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L181-L204
   181  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   182  readback of an expression handle. -/
   183  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   184    | 0, _ => none
   185    | f + 1, i =>
   186      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   187        match v with
   188        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   189        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   190        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   191        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   192        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   193        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   194        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   195        | .letE ty w b =>
   196          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   197        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   198        | .proj n k e =>
   199          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   200  
   201  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:256-375 Expr — the readback of an
   202  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   203  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   204    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds 2^27 entries, so a handle's 27-bit index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation** (`Bridge/Rel.lean`'s `RelE` family),
    26     never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`), because a bare `throw` in
    30     `StateT σ (Except ε)` leaves universe metavariables in the verification
    31     conditions.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L55-L71
    55  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    56  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    57  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    58  
    59  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    60  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    61  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    62  
    63  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    64  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    65  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    66  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    67  inversion). -/
    68  def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
    69      Prop :=
    70    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    71      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

    49  /-! ## The core grade -/
    50  
    51  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step
    52  preserves the whole checking invariant, by `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s
    53  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one
    54  and keep its own hypothesis. -/
    55  theorem PStep.toCore {μ : CheckMode} {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} {s s' : AState}
    56      (h : PStep s s') (hc : CheckOK μ env fe s) : CoreStep μ env fe s s' :=
    57    ⟨hc.monoF h.ok h.ext h.cframe h.pins, h.ext, h.pins⟩
    58  
    59  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/Cached/SimC.lean:366 SimC — **the CORE grade's
    60  statement**: the same at a function that calls the knot, so the invariant is
    61  `CheckOK` and the frame is `CoreStep`.  The pure side's fuel existential lives
    62  inside `R`, as `Bridge/Core/Knot.lean`'s `SimE` has it. -/
    63  def CSpec (μ : CheckMode) (env : Env) (fe : IFEnv) {α : Type}
    64      (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) : Prop :=
    65    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), CheckOK μ env fe s₀ → P s₀.store →
    66      c s₀ = .ok (r, s') → CoreStep μ env fe s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L118-L164
   118  /-! ## The spines -/
   119  
   120  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   121  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   122  
   123  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   124  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   125  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   126  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   127  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   128      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   129      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   130        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   131    intro n
   132    induction n with
   133    | zero =>
   134      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   135      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   136      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   137      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   138    | succ n ih =>
   139      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   140      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   141      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   142      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   143      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   144      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   145      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   146      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   147      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   148          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   149            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   150        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   151        congr 1
   152        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   153        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   154        congr 1
   155        omega
   156      rw [hkey]
   157      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   158  
   159  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   160      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   161    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   162    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   163    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   164    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd
